anatomy.intro: Terminal rosettes make leafy crowns at the ends of a branching framework.

parts.function: Fleshy blades combine green and yellow areas with colored margins.
parts.label: Variegated leaf

parts.function: The youngest leaves cluster at the growing tip.
parts.label: Rosette center

parts.function: Older stem sections hold each rosette above the ground.
parts.label: Woody branch

parts.function: Another growing tip adds a new leafy crown to the shrub.
parts.label: Side rosette

flowers.text: Aeoniums produce clusters of small star-shaped flowers above a mature rosette. That crown dies after flowering, while the other crowns of a branching plant can continue growing.

growth.note: Older leaves fall as new ones develop, naturally exposing the stems below the rosettes; sudden collapse or widespread soft leaves deserve a closer inspection.

stages.text: Young central leaves spread into successive rings.
stages.title: Expand a rosette

stages.text: Stems lengthen and carry additional rosettes.
stages.title: Branch and lift

stages.text: A flowering rosette finishes its life while other branches can persist.
stages.title: Flower one crown

habitat.text: Aeonium haworthii is native to Tenerife in the Canary Islands, where it grows as a subtropical succulent subshrub. The cultivated Dream Color form brings yellow, green and pink-red tones to that branching shape. Older leaves gradually fall away, leaving visible stems topped by living rosettes.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria pulidonis
lookalikes.text: Both have colored rosettes, but this aeonium develops conspicuous woody branches with crowns at their tips; pulidonis stays lower and has thicker blue-grey leaves.

mature.text: RHS lists about 0.1–0.5 m in height and spread for the variegated pinwheel. Expect a branched cluster of crowns rather than one permanently flat rosette; pot conditions affect the eventual scale.
